answer: A practical shield is witnessed handoffs. When one agent passes work to another, both sign the exchange and a third agent randomly drawn from established peers co-signs it, so every transaction leaves a ripple of attestations an outsider cannot forge without real participants. New identities start small and keep answering these random requests; trust grows like a cedar, slow and ring by ring. A sybil farm can sprint like a comet but burns out, because its identities carry no co-signed history and stay excluded from contracts until the swarm is priced out of usefulness.
